steps.hints: ❓ Does the [repeat] loop run the correct number of times to loop through each image in the clamList array?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja: 

❓ Which block determines how many sprites will appear on the screen?

❓ How many values are in the clamList array?


Solution: 

The parameter in the [repeat] loop should be changed from “4” to “3”.
steps.instructions:
When the project runs, there’s an error in the code!


Fix the bugs in the code so that the project is able to run and 3 clamshells appear on screen.

subgroups.introduction:
Oh no - these programs aren’t working! Problems in code are called bugs. Find and fix the bugs in the code in each section!


Fix the bugs in the code so that the correct number of sprites appear on the screen and the user answers questions based on their memory!

validationItems.text: Parameter in [repeat] loop is changed from “4” to “3”.
validationItems.failureText: Check the parameter in the [repeat] loop.

subgroups.name: solve 2

steps.hints: ❓ Does the variable controlling the column position of the clamShell change with each loop?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja: 

❓ How many times should the [columnNumber] change, so that all 3 clamshells appear in different tilemap columns?

❓ Which block causes code to run multiple times in a program?


Solution: 

The [change [variable] by] block should be moved inside the [repeat] loop, underneath the [place sprite on top of] block.
steps.instructions:
When the project runs, all of the clamshells appear in the same column of the tilemap.


Fix the bugs in the code so that 3 clamshells appear on the screen in different tilemap columns.

subgroups.introduction:
Oh no - these programs aren’t working! Problems in code are called bugs. Find and fix the bugs in the code in each section!


Fix the bugs in the code so that the correct number of sprites appear on the screen and the user answers questions based on their memory!

validationItems.text: [change [variable] by] block is placed underneath the [place sprite on top of] block in the [repeat] loop.
validationItems.failureText: Check the placement of the [change [variable] by] block.

subgroups.name: solve 3

steps.hints: ❓ Does the conditional’s <0=0> comparison blocks check for the correct value?
steps.senseiHelp:
Ask the ninja: 

❓ Which array of sprites should be used to check the answer for each question?


Solution: 

The (array of sprites of kind) blocks should be swapped, so that the sprite kind matches the question asked.
steps.instructions:
When the project asks how many fish of each kind appeared on the screen, the game ends in a loss even when the question is answered correctly.


Fix the bugs in the code so that the game ends in a win when the user response matches the number of fish of a certain kind on the screen.

subgroups.title: Debugging Repeat Loops

subgroups.introduction:
Oh no - these programs aren’t working! Problems in code are called bugs. Find and fix the bugs in the code in each section!


Fix the bugs in the code so that the correct number of sprites appear on the screen and the user answers questions based on their memory!

validationItems.text: [array of sprites of kind] blocks swapped in (length of array) blocks, so that the sprite kind matches the question asked.
validationItems.failureText: Check to make sure the correct sprite kind is selected in the (array of sprites of kind) blocks.

attributes.description: You’ve reached Level 4 of Orange Belt! In this level, you’ll learn more about repeat and for loops. A loop is a chunk of code that repeats until a specific condition is met. You’ll use what you already know about variables and arrays to create loops that respond to specific conditions. Here are the achievements you’ll unlock in Level #4:

badges.title: Deja Vu
badges.description: Use different types of loops to repeat code in a project.

badges.title: Once More, With Feeling
badges.description: Use a repeat loop to repeat code a given number of times.

badges.title: Yearbook
badges.description: Create and use an array of sprites.

badges.title: Roll Call
badges.description: Use a for element of loop to make something happen to each item in an array.

badges.title: Freeze Tag
badges.description: Use a pause in a project.

badges.title: Button Down
badges.description: Check if a button is being pressed before making something happen in a project.
